Cluster_PKM_1.paragraph: Key regulators such as *EGLN1, EGLN3, HILPDA, ARNTL2, VEGFA*, and *MIR210HG* indicate robust engagement of the hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) pathway. These factors mediate the transcription of genes involved in anaerobic metabolism, angiogenesis, and cellular survival. The presence of *BNIP3, BNIP3L*, and *NDRG1* supports pro-survival adaptations under low oxygen tension, including autophagy and mitochondrial regulation.

Cluster_PKM_2.paragraph: The set includes multiple enzymes driving glycolysis and diverting carbon flux from mitochondrial respiration (*PFKFB3, PFKFB4, PDK1, PDK3, HK1, ALDOC, ENO2, G6PD, IDH3A/B/G, SDHA/C, OGDH, CS, GOT2*). These act synergistically to reduce oxygen consumption and enhance lactate production, ensuring energy production under hypoxia. *TXN, PRDX3, and NQO1* participate in maintaining redox homeostasis during this metabolic transition.

Cluster_PKM_3.paragraph: Proteins such as *VCL, FLNA, ACTR2/3, MYH9, TUBA4A, TLN1, RHOA, IQGAP1, S100A4, ARPC2, DIAPH1, CTNNA1, VIM* are involved in actin filament organization, microtubule dynamics, and focal adhesion turnover. These changes promote cell migration, invasion, and plasticity—a response consistent with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) under hypoxic stress.
